title: INDICATE chooses Flower SuperGrid for intensive-care AI across Europe
summary: INDICATE has chosen Flower SuperGrid to support collaborative AI research across European intensive care.
body_markdown:
INDICATE has chosen[Flower SuperGrid](https://flower.ai/enterprise) to support collaborative AI research across European intensive care. Bringing together[15 data providers across 12 countries](https://indicate-europe.eu/news/mie-2026-standardizing-icu-data-across-europe-the-indicate-minimal-data-dictionary/) and backed by a[€10 million European Commission grant](https://indicate-europe.eu/news/intensive-cares-in-europe-connect-data/) , the initiative is building infrastructure for hospitals to develop and evaluate AI together while keeping patient data within their own institutions.


The planned integration of SuperGrid will bring Flower's collaborative AI platform and technical expertise into that infrastructure. It will help hospitals learn from clinical experience across institutions and national borders while preserving local control of patient data.


## Developing intensive-care AI across hospitals


For particular conditions and patient groups, a single hospital may have too few relevant cases to train and evaluate an AI model. A model that performs well at one institution also needs to be assessed across other hospitals and patient populations before considering wider clinical use.


This is especially relevant in neonatal and pediatric intensive care, where individual hospitals may have relatively small patient populations. Collaboration allows researchers to draw on data from more patients and assess how models perform across different care settings.


One of INDICATE's[planned research use cases](https://indicate-europe.eu/use-cases/prediction-of-neonatal-and-pediatric-sepsis/) is evaluating an early sepsis detection model for newborns and children. The model uses patient characteristics and bedside monitoring data to estimate sepsis risk. Researchers plan to assess its performance across hospitals, investigate adaptation to local settings, and establish ongoing evaluation and retraining.


Federated learning provides a way to train models across institutions without pooling their raw patient records in a central database. It allows researchers to learn from distributed clinical experience while hospitals continue to manage their own data.


## Bringing collaborative AI into practice


SuperGrid provides a platform for connecting participating sites and organizing collaborative AI workloads. For INDICATE, the self-hosted deployment will allow the consortium to operate that platform within its own infrastructure.


Flower Labs will provide the SuperGrid software, deployment guidance and product support. INDICATE and its partners will operate the infrastructure and connect participating hospitals' local data environments. This combines Flower's expertise in collaborative AI with the consortium's clinical knowledge, data infrastructure and institutional governance.


That support matters as the work moves from research plans into implementation. Connecting institutions requires attention to the environments in which the software will run, how participating sites join the collaboration, and how the platform will be operated over time.


> No hospital should have to build AI from its own experience alone. With INDICATE, we're connecting expertise across Europe so hospitals can learn together, keep control of their data, and advance intensive-care research.
>
>
> **Chong Shen Ng, Flower Labs**


The agreement follows discussions at INDICATE's consortium meeting in Rome, where Chong Shen introduced Flower and demonstrated how researchers can develop AI collaboratively without centralizing patient data.


## A European network spanning 12 countries


INDICATE's wider programme spans six clinical use cases. Its ambition is to establish sustainable European research infrastructure that can support collaboration beyond an individual study.


Choosing Flower SuperGrid is a concrete step towards that ambition. The planned integration will give the consortium a supported platform for collaborative model development, with participating institutions retaining responsibility for their data and infrastructure.


For other organizations pursuing AI across hospitals, research centres or partner networks, the opportunity is to draw on experience distributed across institutions while keeping control of their data and infrastructure.


[Read INDICATE's announcement about the collaboration.](https://indicate-europe.eu/news/indicate-and-flower-labs-join-forces-to-advance-federated-learning-in-intensive-care-research/)
